scan_metadata.analyst_note: Competitive-benchmarking discovery pass for African Grocery Store across the Kansas City MO-KS retail catchment. 10 Google Maps label sweeps (metro centroid plus five corridor centroids), 12 place-detail retrievals, 6 indexed web searches for cross-platform and directory evidence, and one Yelp category page read through search snippets. 28 qualifying storefronts recorded across 12 corridors; 16 out-of-scope businesses excluded with reasons. Gold-standard gates were evaluated on Google for all 28 and on Yelp/Facebook only where evidence was observed; Apple Maps, Bing and BBB were not queried and are recorded not_checked rather than absent. 99 of the 118 grid ZIPs were not opened as independent sweep units and are recorded not_executed — the coverage claim is verified_partial, not a market census.
scan_metadata.geography_grid_derivation: ZIP set and adjacent municipalities were copied verbatim from the cached market grid, which derives them from the Kansas City city boundary plus contiguous incorporated suburbs sharing ZIPs, plus the arterial corridors where category evidence had previously been observed. Sweep units were executed at metro centroid (12z) and at corridor centroids (13z-15z) rather than per ZIP; the ledger records that distinction explicitly.
scan_metadata.google_maps_ground_truth: unavailable — the prompt reported no Google Maps ground-truth signal (level: latest), so corpus fields are marked not_measured rather than inferred. Live Google Maps queries were run directly for this pass and their results are recorded as observed evidence.

category_definition: A walk-in food retailer whose physical shelves carry groceries imported from or characteristic of African countries or African diaspora cuisines. Qualification is decided on assortment evidence — named products, product-region statements, shelf photography or reported stock — not on the business name, a platform category label, or halal status. Subcategories observed in this market: East African / Habesha and Somali groceries (Baraka Market, Mogadisho Market, Jubba Valley, Afro Ethiopia, Fundisha, Hilaal); West African and Ivorian/Ghanaian/Nigerian groceries (Ivoire African Market, Universal Tropical Market, VJ Tropical Market, Ej African Market); pan-African and Caribbean hybrids (Crossland International Market, Pan Afro-Caribbean International Market, O The World Tropical Market); and importer-operated retail (Global Market / New Century Imports, Buwen's African Imports). Business models are product retail throughout: a storefront with shelving, a checkout and posted hours. Three variants sit at the edge of the category — grocery-with-kitchen hybrids (Jay's Grocery & Restaurant, Jubba Valley Market & Kitchen, Al Habashi Mart's sibling restaurant), grocery-plus-goods stores that also sell fabric, shea butter, hair care or clothing (Crossland, Safari Mart, Universal Tropical Market, Buwen's), and a butcher-and-spice format inside a halal grocery (Barakah Halal Market). Excluded from the qualifying set: restaurants serving African cuisine without retail shelves, African goods stores that sell no groceries, halal markets with no African assortment evidence, wholesalers and manufacturers, and one permanently closed storefront.
geographic_classification_notes: inside_city = physically within Kansas City, MO limits. adjacent_city = an immediately contiguous incorporated municipality in the same retail catchment: Gladstone (shares ZIP 64118 with Kansas City), Riverside, Independence, Grandview, Raytown, and Kansas City, KS. metro_area = the broader catchment across the state line: Overland Park, Olathe, Shawnee, Lenexa. No candidate fell outside_market within the 25-mile radius. The observed geography is two dense clusters plus scattered nodes, not one continuous corridor. The Independence Avenue cluster (64106/64124) holds 10 qualifying storefronts within roughly a mile — Baraka, Ej, Hilaal, Jay's, Al Halal, Al Rahaman, Huda Food, Mogadisho, Pichenafrican, and Crossland at the City Market end. The North Oak Trafficway cluster (64118, spanning Kansas City and Gladstone) holds 5 — Universal Tropical Market, African Market Universal Tropical, African International Market, Tour of Africa and Barakah Halal Market — plus Afro Ethiopia on NW Vivion in Riverside. Single-storefront nodes: Ivoire African Market on Wornall (Waldo), VJ Tropical Market on Troost, Pan Afro-Caribbean in Grandview, O The World in Raytown, Buwen's in Independence, Global Market in Overland Park, Safari Mart in Olathe, Fundisha in Shawnee, and Sankofa plus Anointed in Kansas City, KS. The Lee's Summit / Blue Springs / Grain Valley sweep executed empty: no African grocery, market or goods store returned in that quadrant. City Market is a comparator node (Crossland, Al Habashi, plus Asian grocers), not an African-grocery concentration in its own right.
ownership_exclusion_notes: No national chain, national franchise or multi-state regional chain qualified for this category in this market — the category is structurally independent here, and the observed roster is entirely owner-operated single storefronts plus one two-storefront local operation. Universal Tropical Market LLC and African Market Universal Tropical Market are recorded as local_chain: two storefronts on N Oak Trafficway within two miles, with reviews naming the same owner ('AJ') and describing 'several store locations'. suggested_reasons.proposed_label: Duplicate listing splitting the same storefront's reputation
suggested_reasons.proposed_definition: A single walk-in storefront maintains two live platform listings under different brand names, each with its own review corpus, phone number and category set. Neither listing carries the full review depth or the correct category, so the store under-performs in local ranking against competitors with one consolidated profile — and the operator usually does not know both listings exist.
